newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca falls amid drug development doubts.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca falls amid drug development doubts.

text.p: Shares in Zeneca Group Plc lost earlier gains to trade 12-1/2 pence lower at 1,890 after a meeting with the drug company left analysts with doubts over the firm's long-term growth potential.
They said it became clear during the meeting, which just finished, that there will be a significant gap between the first and second wave of new products hitting the market.

The first wave, including migraine drug Zomig and ashtma treatment Accolate, is coming to market about now, but a new generation will not be ripe for sale by 2001 when the patent expires on Zeneca's top-selling treatment, heart drug Zestril.
"There still won't be new products from the second wave of development on the market by that stage (the Zestril patent expiry)," said analyst Nick Wolf at Nomura.
Shares in Zeneca initially rose to reach an intraday peak of 1,938 pence after the company released 1996 results which came in higher then most industry watchers had expected.
Full-year pre-tax profit rose to 975 million stg compared with 619 million stg the previous year.
